column2: How do I see the house in cross-section?
column3: 🏠 House tab → “🧰 House tools” → “✂ Draw the section line”, then two clicks on the plan (the red “A — A” line stays drawn). The section shows the floors, the hatched floor slabs, the cut walls with their doors and windows, the staircase, the roof and the heights; “🖨 Print…”, “⤓ Export as SVG” or “as PNG”.

column2: How do I know the living area of the house, room by room?
column3: 🏠 House tab → “🧰 House tools” → “📐 Areas per room”: each room, each floor and the whole house, on the ground and according to the Carrez law (only where you can stand up, 1.80 m and more). “🧾 In the spreadsheet” opens the same table in the Spreadsheet, with the totals as formulas.

column2: How do I check that the house plan holds up?
column3: 🏠 House tab → “⚠️ Check the plan”: a list in the style of the Database check (🔴 impossible, 🟠 to check, 🟡 curious) — a door wider than its wall or placed on a wall that has gone, a window cut by the floor or under the slope of the roof, a room without a door, a staircase that is too steep (Blondel’s rule) or that does not cut through the floor, a void that opens onto nothing… A click on a line takes you to the object.

column2: How do I see the house change over the years?
column3: Create dated periods (🕰 The periods, 🏠 House tab); “🧰 House tools” then has a “🕰 The year” slider: as you drag it, the plan and the 3D view take the most recent period before that year. “▶ Watch it change” plays through them.

column2: How do I see who lived in a room during the visit?
column3: Click the room → “🕯 Memories of the room” → “The people of the room” (the usual picker, main and secondary, a role on each badge: their bedroom, born here, servant…), then their years. During the visit (🚶 Visit), when you enter the room, a small card shows these people; a click opens their record, “✦” the memories of the room.

column2: How do I prepare a guided tour of the house?
column3: 3D view → “🚶 Visit”: position yourself, look at what should be shown, then “📍 Stop here” and write what is said at that spot. Then, 🏠 House tab → “▶ Guided tour”: you move from one stop to the next by sliding, and the text is read aloud. “✎ The stops” to rewrite or reorder them; “⤓ Tour images” gives one image per stop and the texts, to drop into 🎬 Video editing to make a film.

column2: How do I compare an old photo with the house today?
column3: During the visit, stand where the photo was taken, turn in the same direction, then “📷 Period photo here” and choose the photo (images window). It shows over the 3D view with a “Then ⟷ Now” slider. A 📷 marks it on the plan and in 3D; a click on it takes you back there.

column2: How do I show the hamlet, the farm and its outbuildings?
column3: Draw each building as a house in the list (the barn, the bread oven, the house next door…), then in the main house: 🏠 House → “🏘 Buildings on the land…” → ＋ each building (picker), and set its offset and rotation. They appear in dotted lines on the plan and in 3D in their place. The census household number is noted in the same place.

column2: How do I send the house tour to someone who does not have the app?
column3: 🏠 House tab → “📤 Share the tour”: an .html file to send (e-mail, USB stick). It opens with a double-click in any browser, without the Internet: the house in 3D, its plans and the guided tour, read-only. It contains neither the inhabitants, nor the memories, nor the notes, nor the photos.

column2: Can the house be shown in simple mode?
column3: Yes: Settings → Accessibility → 🧓 Simple mode → “The big buttons” → “＋ Add a tile” → “🏠 The house”, then choose the house. In simple mode, this big button shows the house in 3D turning slowly, with big buttons to turn, move closer, change floor and listen to the guided tour — without being able to change anything.

column2: How do I make the video of the house’s guided tour?
column3: 🏠 House tab → “🧰 House tools” → “🎬 Tour video…” (you need stops: 3D view → 🚶 Visit → 📍 Stop here). Choose the format (landscape, square, portrait) and the opening title: the camera glides from one stop to the next and the text of each stop is shown as a subtitle. “⤓ Export the video” gives an MP4 or WebM file (depending on the computer); “Also keep a copy in the media” stores it with your videos. “⤓ Tour images” is still there for Video editing.

column2: Can I put a glass roof or an exit on a flat roof?
column3: Yes: with a flat roof (Floor tab → 🏠 Roof → Shape “Flat”), the buttons become “＋ Glass roof”, “＋ Roof lantern” (a glazed peak) and “＋ Roof structure” (the small building of the exit onto the roof). Each one can be set (place, crosswise, width, depth) and is visible in 3D and in the section, like the dormers of a sloping roof.

column2: How do I walk around the house in simple mode?
column3: In simple mode’s “🏠 The house”, the “🚶 Walk around inside” button: big buttons ⬆ Forward, ⬇ Back, ⬅ ➡ Turn, ⏫ ⏬ change floor, and “🏠 See the whole house” to go out. No keyboard or mouse needed; nothing can be changed.

column2: How do I show who lived in a room, with their role?
column3: Click the room → “🕯 Memories of the room” → “The people of the room”: the usual picker with the two areas “★ Main” and “☆ Secondary” and a role on each badge (their bedroom, born here, servant… or a free word; a person without a record is possible). The years are noted just below. Roles written before are kept as they are.

column2: How do I measure in the house’s 3D view?
column3: 3D view → “📏 Measure”, then two clicks on the house: the distance, the ground distance and the difference in height. “Dimensions” shows the length of each wall and the ceiling height; “Top”, “Front”, “Side” position the camera. The thickness of the floors between two storeys is set in the Floor tab.

column2: How do I line up a floor with the one below or above?
column3: At the top of the plan, next to the floors: “👻” chooses the floor shown transparently (below, above, both, or none). Its walls and the outline of its rooms are shown in dotted lines, brown for the one below, blue for the one above. The transparency is set in the Floor tab.

column2: How do I move a room with its walls?
column3: Drag the room: its walls (doors and windows included), its furniture and its texts follow; neighbouring walls attached at a corner stretch to stay joined. A wall shared with another room does not move. To move only the floor: ⇧ while dragging, or untick “🔗 Walls and furniture follow the room” in its properties.

column2: How do I get more furniture and objects in the house plan?
column3: “Furniture” tab: 700 objects old and new, sorted by room (Bedroom, Living room, Dining room, Kitchen, Bathroom, Laundry room, Hall, Study, Children, Garage, Garden…) and by kind (Lighting, Decoration, Appliances, Music, Storage, Farm and animals, Structure). Type a word in “Search”: box bed, kneading trough, lamp, guitar, living room, bathroom, toy… (the number of objects found is shown; Esc empties the box). Click on the object: it is placed in the middle of the view. Each object has its real dimensions, its drawing seen from above and its 3D shape; its colour, second colour and material can be changed in “Properties”.

column2: Does the house plan get slow with a lot of furniture?
column3: No: in 3D, each piece of furniture is grouped into a few volumes (one per material), even with 200 objects placed. If the 3D view stays slow on an old computer, untick “All floors” or use “Top”.

column2: How do I create my own object for the house plan?
column3: Furniture → “＋ Create an object”: “Start from an existing object” takes the size, shape and material of a piece from the catalogue (a linen cupboard, a dough bin…), then you change what you want: its name, its category (or a new one), its size in cm, its shape seen from above and in 3D, its material (oak, walnut, cast iron, copper, wicker, earthenware…), its colour and a second colour (legs, handles), its legs, its height from the floor, its direction, its rounded corners, its doors and drawers, its period, and if you like a photo seen from above (from the computer or “🖼️ A photo from the media”). The preview shows the object in 2D and 3D. It is kept for all your houses, in its category and in “My objects”; ✎ to edit or delete it.

column2: How do I put an image in a frame or on a painting in the house (recreate a painter’s studio)?
column3: Choose the frame, the painting, the canvas, the easel, the poster, the mirror or the gallery wall: in its settings, “🖼 Image” section, “🖼 Change” opens the window of images from your media (filtered on the house’s first inhabitant). You can also drag an image from the computer straight onto the object, in the plan or in the 3D view: it goes into the media and is placed on it. A memory attached to the object can serve as the image. Settings: fill, fit or centre, drag and zoom in the preview to crop, rotate by 90°, mat and frame (colour, width). Gallery wall: one image per frame (badges 1 to 6). The house only keeps the media number and its settings; if the image no longer exists, a plain canvas replaces it.

column2: What trade and workshop objects are there in the house plan?
column3: Furniture → “Trades, workshop”: more than 100 objects sorted by trade — painter (studio, field and table easels, stretched canvases from size 6 F to 100 F, stacked canvases, canvas racks, palette, paint box, side table, model’s platform), sculptor, blacksmith and farrier, joiner and cabinet-maker, cooper, wheelwright, shoemaker, tailor and seamstress, weaver, potter, baker, butcher, grocer, apothecary, clockmaker, printer, bookbinder, photographer, schoolteacher, doctor and midwife, barber, miller, winegrower, beekeeper, washerwoman, lacemaker, instrument maker, notary and town hall, post office, miner, fisherman, sailor, rural policeman. Look for the trade (“baker”, “clockmaker”…) in the Furniture search box.

column2: How do I find antique furniture and objects from the past?
column3: Furniture → tick “🕰 Antique only”: only furniture and things from the past remain (linen cupboard, dough bin, longcase clock, Breton dresser, settle chest, box bed, wooden cradle, spinning wheel, butter churn, oil lamp, Godin stove, andirons, mantelpiece, treadle sewing machine, school bench…), in each category and in the search. Untick to see everything again.

column2: How do I change the material, the legs or the second colour of a piece of furniture already placed?
column3: Click on the furniture → Properties → “🎨 Material, legs, details”: the material (oak, walnut, cherry, cast iron, copper, stone, marble, wicker, straw, earthenware, fabric…), a second colour (legs, handles, trims), legs (straight, turned, ball, glides, castors), rounded corners, the number of doors and drawers (wardrobes, sideboards, chests of drawers) and its period. The 3D view follows straight away.

column2: How do I link a house to people or censuses?
column3: In the house, “House” tab: “＋ An inhabitant…” for a person, “＋ A census…” for one or more censuses (tick “Also add the people of the household” to make them inhabitants in one go). At the top of the tab, “🔗 Linked to” shows everything that is linked; a click opens the record. In Lists → “🏠 Family houses”, “Linked to” shows it too (▦ Cards or ☰ Table).
